transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-10-20 16:00 UTC / Duration 48m
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Marco (Redwood SE), Marcus (HelixForge CTO), Lina (HelixForge NetEng), Aisha (HelixForge Security PM), Tom (HelixForge DevOps)
Deck: HelixForge-onramp-v1.pdf (sent in chat) | Security packet: redwood-security-2026.pdf (link)

[00:00] Jordan (AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, we'll run ~45 minutes — discovery first, then map out next steps. Marcus, do you want to kick off with your main goals?

[00:18] Marcus (CTO): Sure. Our main ask is we want to move inference workloads off our pilot hosted experiments into something that meets our residency and egress controls. We're evaluating Redwood for a private deployment in our AWS account or maybe a dedicated, but residency, encryption, and strict IP allowlisting are musts. We also have multi-region constraints — EU data must stay in eu-west-1 or eu-central-1.

[00:42] Priya (SE): Got it. For Private we typically offer a customer-controlled VPC model where we deploy the inference nodes into a customer VPC and provide private endpoints. Two common patterns: VPC peering (or Transit Gateway) and PrivateLink-style endpoints. Which one is your preference?

[01:05] Lina (NetEng): We prefer Transit Gateway for scale, peering is ok for small test but we need central routing. Also we use AWS Direct Connect to our colo, so minimizing hairpin and egress is important.

[01:20] Marco (SE): Good note. For Transit GW we support advertising routes into the Redwood subnets and we can work with BGP TTL/ASNs — in practice customers map a route table and we advise on IP planning. We'll need a CIDR block for the Redwood nodes and details on overlapping address spaces.

[01:45] Aisha (Security PM): A few compliance Qs up front: SOC2 status, KMS integrations, HSM for keys, and audit logs. Also do you support bringing our KMS keys for model encryption and log encryption?

[02:05] Jordan (AE): Yes we support customer-managed KMS in Private deployments. We'll share the security packet, but briefly we do integrate with AWS KMS/HSM for secrets and have audit log forwarding. Our hosted product already has SOC2; private deployments are covered under our enterprise agreement and we can provide an architecture for key management.

[02:30] Marcus (CTO): Region question — if we want eu-west-1 only for customer data, does that mean Redwood will spin up nodes in eu-west-1 and not cross-replicate to US?

[02:45] Priya (SE): Correct, you can pin the control plane to a region and we can restrict egress so data never leaves the pinned region. There are caveats with control/control-plane interactions; if you want a fully air-gapped control plane we'd discuss Private mode where the control plane is customer-managed. But for typical Private we can enforce region residency and avoid cross-region KV cache replication.

[03:10] Tom (DevOps): On egress - we need static egress IPs to allowlist downstream APIs. How do you handle NAT/Egress IP allocation?

[03:25] Marco (SE): We can assign a set of NAT gateways or egress IPs from your VPC; alternatively Redwood-managed egress is possible but for your use case we recommend customer-managed NAT so you control IPs. We'll document required ports and FQDNs to allowlist.

[03:48] Lina (NetEng): Any requirements around MTU, TCP keepalives? We run heavy KV replication across a private link to our infra.

[04:00] Priya (SE): No special MTU normally, but for on-prem WANs sometimes we adjust. We'll provide recommended TCP keepalive and idle timeout values. Also we support prefix/KV cache configurations to reduce repeated data transfer.

[04:18] Marcus (CTO): How about latency SLAs? If we route to eu-west-1 nodes we need tail latency under 100ms p95 for short-chat workloads otherwise we'll reconsider.

[04:36] Jordan (AE): For Dedicated we provide latency SLAs; Private will be similar depending on your instance types and placement. We'll propose GPU profiles and expected p95 numbers in the SOW. We can also run a benchmark PoC to validate.

[04:53] Aisha (Security PM): A few more: SSO (SAML/SCIM), RBAC integration with our IdP, and ability to configure audit retention.

[05:05] Priya (SE): We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning; audit logs can be forwarded to your CloudWatch or SIEM. Retention windows are configurable in Private.

[05:20] Lina (NetEng): What's the recommended IP range sizing for the Redwood nodes? We need to avoid overlap with our Kubernetes pod CIDRs and our Transit GW.

[05:35] Marco (SE): We typically ask for a /20 to start for medium workloads; for large scale we recommend /18. But you can start smaller and expand. Critical: no overlapping with your existing VPCs or on-prem prefixes. Provide current CIDRs and Transit attachments and we'll produce a sample IP plan.

[05:58] Marcus (CTO): If we run a mixed fleet — some workloads in Dedicated and some in Private — can we route between them? We're thinking of a hybrid where sensitive data goes to Private, and lower sensitivity research uses Hosted.

[06:15] Priya (SE): Yes, policy-based routing is possible. You can route by model tag, route rules, or by customer token. We also support automatic fallback to hosted variants if private capacity is exhausted, but for strict residency you'd want to disable fallback.

[06:38] Tom (DevOps): Any constraints on pre-shared certificates or mTLS for node-to-node? We require mutual TLS for all service-to-service comms within our network.

[06:50] Marco (SE): Redwood supports mTLS between control and nodes; for Private deployments we can accept customer-provided certs or help generate them. We'll include cert rotation and TTL recommendations.

[07:05] Jordan (AE): Quick question on timeline — what's your internal deadline for production rollout?

[07:12] Marcus (CTO): End of Q1 2027 for pilot completion, production in Q2. So we want a PoC in the next two weeks to validate networking and residency.

[07:25] Priya (SE): Sounds doable. For PoC we usually do a 2-week network/latency validation — we ask for a VPC peering/transit attachment and sample traffic to run inference and measure p95 and egress. We'll also run a security checklist.

[07:40] Aisha (Security PM): Will you provide a signed NDA or do you need ours?

[07:45] Jordan (AE): We can sign yours; Jordan to follow up with legal. We'll also attach our security packet and SOC2 letter.

[08:00] Marco (SE): Diving a bit deeper — Lina, can you describe your Transit GW architecture and the current route tables, and whether you use separate route tables per account?

[08:18] Lina (NetEng): We have a single Transit GW with multiple attachments: two prod VPCs in eu-west-1, one shared services VPC, and a Direct Connect to our colo. Route tables are per-attachment currently. We can export the route table.

[08:34] Marco (SE): That's perfect. For scale we'll suggest a dedicated attachment for Redwood nodes with a clear route table and a /22 CIDR ideally. We'll also need your BGP ASN for the Direct Connect peering.

[08:50] Marcus (CTO): What about IP egress for analytics? We ingest logs into our analytics cluster; can you push logs to our S3 in-region without leaving eu-west-1?

[09:05] Priya (SE): Yes — all logs and data egress can be kept in-region. We'll set the S3 endpoints and ensure no replication. We'll include config snippets in the checklist.

[09:22] Marcus (CTO): Any surprises around compliance? For example, data residency plus model updates — do model weights ever leave the region during updates or retraining?

[09:35] Priya (SE): For Private deployments, model artifacts are stored in your region; if you choose Redwood-managed updates, we coordinate to keep artifacts in-region. If you want full control, you can host artifact storage in your account and we will pull from there. We can also sign an addendum about artifact residency.

[09:58] Aisha (Security PM): What about vulnerability scanning and patch windows? We need maintenance windows and CVE reports.

[10:10] Marco (SE): We'll provide weekly patch windows for non-prod and scheduled windows for prod. CVE notifications and a PSIRT contact are included in enterprise support. We'll confirm SLA details in the SOW.

[10:30] Jordan (AE): Let's talk briefly about cost: Dedicated reserved capacity vs Private in-customer VPC — high level differences?

[10:40] Marco (SE): Dedicated means Redwood reserves GPU pools in our managed infra, good for predictable throughput. Private puts nodes in your VPC so you pay for infra in your account plus Redwood platform fees. We'll sketch a cost comparison and a pilot pricing model.

[11:00] Lina (NetEng): For the PoC, what ports and FQDNs do we need to open?

[11:08] Priya (SE): We'll provide a concise allowlist: control-plane endpoints, container registry endpoints (if we pull images), KMS and S3 endpoints, and NTP. We'll include specific ports (HTTPS 443, BGP 179 for Direct Connect optional, SSH 22 for debug if enabled).

[11:30] Marcus (CTO): For pilot scale — how many qps or concurrency should we plan? We have a bursty API with peaks 400 rps short-chat and baseline 50 rps.

[11:45] Marco (SE): We'll map that to GPU types; likely need multiple smaller GPU instances with autoscaling. We'll include concurrency guidance and token cost estimations in the follow-up.

[12:05] Aisha (Security PM): We require logs forwarded to our SIEM with minimal PII. Do you redact PII at rest?

[12:20] Priya (SE): We support configurable logging levels; PII redaction is possible via the request routing and logs can be obfuscated. For Private we recommend pushing logs into your own S3 and SIEM to avoid storing unredacted copies in vendor storage.

[12:40] Jordan (AE): Ok, time check — about 15 minutes left. Let's do a short recap and firm next steps.

[12:50] Jordan (AE): Priya, what do you need to run the PoC network test?

[12:55] Priya (SE): We need: 1) Transit GW attachment details and BGP ASN; 2) Desired Redwood node CIDR (/22 recommended); 3) Allowlist for egress destinations; 4) Point of contact for AWS account access or a cross-account role; 5) Preferred region pinning (you said eu-west-1).

[13:18] Marcus (CTO): We'll provide the route table exports and ASN. We prefer a cross-account role with least privilege for the PoC.

[13:30] Jordan (AE): Great. Action items captured — Jordan will send high-level pricing and SOW; Priya will upload checklist and sample IP plan; Marcus/Lina/Aisha to provide network tables and compliance matrix.

[13:45] Marco (SE): Final note — some customers opt for PrivateLink for strict per-service endpoints rather than whole VPC attachments; that reduces blast radius but might be more work to scale. If you want Transit GW for scale, that's the recommended path.

[14:05] Marcus (CTO): We'll evaluate both; thanks.

[14:12] Jordan (AE): I'll follow up within 24 hours with the security packet and pricing sketch and we'll aim to schedule the SE deep dive on 2026-10-29. Everyone good?

[14:20] Aisha (Security PM): Good. Also please include sample SIEM mapping and retention table.

[14:28] Jordan (AE): Will do. Thanks all — meeting adjourned.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker overlap; some product names transcribed as "Redwood PrivateLink" or "Redwood transit" interchangeably. Misspellings observed for ASN as "A-S-N" and KV cache sometimes transcribed as "K-V cash".

Recap (end): Redwood to share Private onramp checklist, sample IP plan, SOW/pricing; HelixForge to share route tables, ASN, compliance docs; SE deep dive and PoC tentatively scheduled.
